atlas_home_region_card.compact: A smooth late-1970s/early-1980s studio-pop road of jazz chords, R&B-schooled vocals, elite session playing, and immaculate adult-radio polish.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It turns professionalism into a vibe. The lane is a masterclass in session-player precision, adult-contemporary crossover, blue-eyed soul influence, and pop arrangements where nothing sounds accidental.

region_scene_page.compact: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound.
region_scene_page.standard: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound. Steely Dan's Hey Nineteen, The Doobie Brothers' Minute by Minute, Kenny Loggins' This Is It, and Ambrosia's Biggest Part of Me give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound. The groove is clean, the chords are richer than standard soft rock, and the musicianship is almost invisible because it is so controlled. Steely Dan's Hey Nineteen, The Doobie Brothers' Minute by Minute, Kenny Loggins' This Is It, and Ambrosia's Biggest Part of Me give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.

mission_detail_history_module.compact: What this route tests: A smooth late-1970s/early-1980s studio-pop road of jazz chords, R&B-schooled vocals, elite session playing, and immaculate adult-radio polish.
mission_detail_history_module.standard: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound. Steely Dan, Michael McDonald-era Doobie Brothers, Christopher Cross, Toto, Kenny Loggins, and related artists make rock feel sleek, harmonically expensive, and rhythmically relaxed. It helps place this road in a broader music-history context.
mission_detail_history_module.deep: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound. Steely Dan, Michael McDonald-era Doobie Brothers, Christopher Cross, Toto, Kenny Loggins, and related artists make rock feel sleek, harmonically expensive, and rhythmically relaxed. It turns professionalism into a vibe. The lane is a masterclass in session-player precision, adult-contemporary crossover, blue-eyed soul influence, and pop arrangements where nothing sounds accidental.
